newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF AC MILAN PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF AC MILAN PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of AC Milan players most likely to play in Sunday's Italian serie A match against Sampdoria:

Sebastiano Rossi, goalkeeper, age 32. First choice keeper since 1992. Fan's scapegoat for Milan's recent fall from grace. Asked to be dropped after blunder against Rosenberg put Milan out of European Cup. Now back but yet to recover confidence. Went record 929 minutes without being beaten in 1994/95 season.

Paolo Maldini, defender, 28. Son of new Italy coach Cesare. Product of Milan youth team. Fixture in senior side since debut at age of 16 in 1985. Reputation as best-attacking full-back in world undermined by recent poor form. Good looks also put out of joint by recent fracture to cheek bone. Radio disc jockey in his spare time.

Michael Reiziger, defender, 23. Signed from Ajax Amsterdam last year but struggled to win place in Tabarez's first team line-up. Departure of Christian Panucci for Real Madrid after public falling out with Arrigo Sacchi has given this Dutch international a regular first-team spot.

Francesco Coco, defender, 19. Coveted as natural replacement for Maldini at left-back if, as expected, the latter takes Franco Baresi's place in the centre of defence next season. Another Milan youth team product.

Franco Baresi, defender, 36. Milan's longest serving player who announces in April whether he will retire at season's end. Symbol of success under Silvio Berlusconi, lifting three European Cups and five league titles in 10 years. Despite injury and Milan's poor form, "Kaiser Franz" reputation remains intact.

Alessandro Costacurta, defender 30. Good man-to-man marker but weak link in Milan's defence this season and dropped by Sacchi last Sunday. Rumoured to be leaving at end of season. National coach Cesare Maldini looks like persisting with him for World Cup qualifier against England on February 12.

Marcel Desailly, defender, 28. With Marseille side that defeated Milan in 1993 European Cup final. At Milan six months later at Baresi's request to fill holding role between midfield and defence. Superb centre-half in France side, "the Rock" shudders at the thought of implementing Sacchi's off-side trap.

Demetrio Albertini, midfielder, 28. Reared in Milan youth team but farmed out to Padua for season before earning first-team place in 1991. Favourite of Sacchi, who turned him into national team's playmaker. Packs powerful shot and takes penalty.

Zvonimir Boban, midfielder, 28. Started with Dynamo Zagreb. Signed for Milan in 1991 but lent to Bari for season. Admired by Sacchi who sees him as the new Carlo Ancelotti. Croat captain. National hero after protecting fans from truncheon wielding police in last Yugoslav Cup final. Keen chess player.

Edgar Davids, midfielder, 23. Signed from Ajax after impressing Milan with versatile performance in 1995 European Cup win. Lost automatic place in Sacchi's side due to lack of tactical discipline, including tendency to dwell on ball. Still to conquer feisty temperament. Nicknamed "Pitbull terrier".

Jesper Blomqvist, midfielder, 22. Caught eye in Gothenburg's win over Italian champions in this season's European Cup before joining Desailly and Davids in Milan's "if you can't beat them, buy them" club on four-year contract. Viewed as natural replacement for Roberto Donadoni. Graduate in maths.

Stefano Eranio, midfielder, 30. Started career with home-town Genoa, reaching 1992 UEFA Cup semifinals before joining Milan. Aggressive midfielder with fierce shot, recently won extension to contract after threatening to join Sampdoria.

Massimo Ambrosini, midfielder, 19. Promising midfielder tipped for international honours. Has reportedly impressed Sacchi with defensive qualities but needs to improve play-making skills. Already key member of Italy's Under-21 team.

Dejan Savicevic, midfielder, 30. Montenegrin signed from Red Star Belgrade in 1992. Fell out with coach Fabio Capello and only took first-team place after Berlusconi intervened. Nicknamed "The Genie" for ability to conjure up openings. Not a Sacchi favourite. Tipped to leave Milan at end of season.

George Weah, striker, 30. Liberian who spent six seasons in France before moving to Milan and playing key role in 1995/96 title win. Last season's World player of the year. Natural replacement for Dutchman Marco Van Basten. Marred reputation by head-butting Porto's Jorge Costa after European Cup match. Recently out of action with ankle injury.

Cristophe Dugarry, striker, 24. Dugarry scored in Milan's UEFA Cup exit to Bordeaux last season, earning a three-year contract. Knee operation delayed debut until October. Weah's injury has given French international extended run in first-team. Never-say-die attitude has won Sacchi's favour.

Marco Simone, striker, 28. Complete centre-forward. Slick on turn with eye for opportunist goal. Waited until this season to shake off reputation as Supersub and claim first-team place in Tabarez's side. But loss of form and injury has kept Simone out of Sacchi's side.

Roberto Baggio, striker, 29. Fought off poor form and claims that he was finished to win place in Tabarez's team only for Sacchi to put him back on the bench. But since changing room row with man who also dropped him from Italy side, Baggio has fought back into side. Former European footballer of the year.
